messages:
ravi_k: spike finding : we should expose a /capabilities endpoint on adapters so control-plane can probe what runtime actually supports (kv-cache, batch-shape, hsm-integration). runtime can return stable version + opt-ins.

elaine: good. makes routing decisions easier. what's the contract shape? simple list of strings or do we need richer signals (latency cost)?

ravi_k: propose small schema: `capabilities.v1` -> { version, features:[{name, stable:boolean, reason_if_unavailable}], perf_hints: optional map }. keep it minimal so embedded devices (on-prem) can implement easily.

kevin: perf_hints are important. some runtimes support small-batch fast path, others favor large-batch throughput. control-plane needs a numeric throughput_hint (tokens/sec) and p99_latency_ms.

tom_s: security note: the probe must be authenticated and rate-limited. private deployments might object to capability probes from public control-plane. maybe allow a probe_mode: `push` vs `pull` where private adapters push capabilities periodically.

elaine: yes, push-mode for Private/Dedicated, pull-mode for Hosted. also add a signed-etag so we can correlate versions.

ravi_k: another idea: lease tokens for special capabilities. e.g., if adapter exposes `prefetch_keys` it may handover a `capability_lease` that control-plane uses to request short-lived access. avoids storing customer secrets in central service.

kevin: lease model would solve KMS pointer exchange. flow: control-plane requests lease for a route, adapter returns lease_id + ttl + opaque_audience. control-plane attaches lease_id in subsequent calls. runtime validates.

tom_s: operationally we should support lease revocation and rotation. Add `revoke_endpoint` to capability manifest. Also logging for audit trail (who requested lease).

elaine: fallback semantics: if a requested capability is flakey, adapter should return a structured `degradation` object with `code`, `retry_after_sec`, and `granularity` (per-request / per-route). code examples: `TEMP_UNAVAILABLE`, `NOT_SUPPORTED`, `AUTHZ_FAIL`.

ravi_k: agreed. control-plane can then choose: degrade (switch to model without kv-cache), route to hosted, or queue the request. We need policy knobs per customer.

devops-bot: note: CI job created -> `infra/probes/capability-schema-test` link: https://ci/redwood/infra/p/1234 :white_check_mark:

kevin: version negotiation: adapters must publish `api_major` and `api_minor`. mismatch policy: major mismatch = reject; minor mismatch = best-effort with warnings. We'll add a `compatibility_matrix` doc.

tom_s: before we standardize, run small canary: add capability probe to staging adapters only. watch for errors where older adapters return unknown keys. shim strategy: unknown features are ignored with a warning header `X-Adapter-Unknown: <feature>`

elaine: UI/Console impact: show adapter-reported capabilities on route page + last_probed timestamp. allow manual override per-tenant to force route to only use certain capabilities.

ravi_k: migration plan: 1) implement minimal /capabilities on hosted adapter, 2) staging rollouts on dedicated, 3) Private customers get a client library to implement push heartbeat, 4) flip policies after 3 weeks.

kevin: tests: unit for schema parsing, e2e that simulates `NOT_SUPPORTED` and verifies control-plane reroutes. I'll add tickets.

ravi_k: I'll draft an RFC with sample probe payload, lease sequence diagram, and the policy table. ping me edits here.

devops-bot: reminder: arch sync Friday 3pm.
